description: Aggressive runtime repair, evidence capture, before/after comparison, and optional family-validation skills extracted from the clone final-repair stage.

skills.title: Aggressively fix reproducible runtime defects
skills.intent: Treat console errors, broken flows, and runtime crashes as first-class defects while preserving mechanics.
required_actions: Reproduce or localize console/runtime errors.
Fix underlying causes when safe and reload to verify.
Preserve mechanics while repairing code-level blockers.
acceptance_bar: Blocking runtime defects are repaired or explicitly documented.
The game remains the same game after repair.
failure_modes_prevented: Repair passes that rewrite the game instead of fixing it

skills.title: Probe multiple states and protect mobile actionability
skills.intent: Verify real user flows rather than stopping at the first screen.
required_actions: Explore start/play/restart/menu/pause/failure/win paths when present.
Check that controls, CTAs, modals, and overlays are reachable on mobile.
Fix z-index traps, clipped actions, hidden next steps, and tap blockers.
acceptance_bar: The game can be entered, played, and exited through its real states on mobile.
Usability is not the source of difficulty.
failure_modes_prevented: State flows that trap the player

skills.title: Fix deterministically, ignore non-blocking noise
skills.intent: Keep final repair focused on real blockers instead of endless speculative cleanup.
required_actions: Ignore non-blocking external/generated media 404 noise unless it breaks code or required visibility.
Only apply deterministic asset/CDN fixes when the correct route is known.
Prefer minimal surgical repairs over broad redesign.
acceptance_bar: The repair pass focuses on actual blockers and visible defects.
Optional network noise does not derail validation.
failure_modes_prevented: Wasting the repair loop on harmless media fetch failures

skills.title: Repair touch/click lifecycle breakage with a known safe pattern
skills.intent: Preserve the concrete mobile-tap anti-pattern lesson from the final repair source library.
required_actions: Watch for global touch suppression that breaks button click synthesis on mobile.
Scope gesture prevention to active gameplay surfaces instead of the whole document.
Keep UI buttons, menus, dialogs, and overlays on native tap/click paths whenever possible.
acceptance_bar: Start, continue, restart, and other CTA paths work on mobile tap as well as desktop click.
Gesture handling is scoped and explainable.
failure_modes_prevented: Global touchstart preventDefault breaking CTA buttons
Late QA rediscovering known mobile input traps

skills.title: Capture real screenshots and compare before vs after
skills.intent: Make the super operator prove visual/runtime change with evidence instead of claims.
required_actions: Capture before-state evidence when the original surface can be inspected.
Capture after-state evidence for entry, live play, and reachable terminal or modal states.
Write a before/after comparison note tying observations to actual screenshots.
acceptance_bar: The transformation is evidenced visually and operationally.
Comparisons describe real deltas rather than subjective hype.
failure_modes_prevented: No proof that the remix changed meaningfully

skills.title: Keep final contracts aligned with actual QA
skills.intent: Ensure the QA phase emits honest structured outputs and risk notes.
required_actions: Report errors found and fixed, states observed, screenshots captured, and remaining limitations.
Keep contract status aligned with the actual repair outcome.
Call out remaining non-blocking risks explicitly.
acceptance_bar: The final report matches what was actually validated.
Consumers can tell what is solved versus what remains risky.

skills.title: Validate level/file families only when they exist
use_when: Only if the v5 output produces multiple playable surface variants such as index_level_01.html through index_level_05.html.
skills.intent: Preserve the multilevel QA value embedded in the source library without forcing it when the v5 output is a single canonical game.
required_actions: Use the canonical surface as the structural and behavioral reference.
Validate each derived surface for boot, startability, direct-open compatibility, and mobile safety.
Check shared bugs at shared sources first and validate visual progression coherence across the family.
acceptance_bar: Variant families are coherent, playable, and visually progressive when present.
No family drift is accepted as an accidental side effect.
failure_modes_prevented: Adjacent levels with no coherent progression

skills.title: Audit visual DNA and staged progression when families exist
use_when: Only if the v5 output emits multiple progression-linked playable surfaces.
skills.intent: Carry forward the multilevel QA requirement to reason about shared visual DNA and staged escalation rather than only checking bootability.
required_actions: Define the stable visual DNA that makes the family recognizable as one game.
Describe how later variants escalate atmosphere, density, and tension without breaking readability.
Use the visual progression plan as a reference when deciding whether adjacent levels are drifting or too interchangeable.
acceptance_bar: Variant families express both mechanical and visual progression coherently.
Later variants remain siblings, not unrelated reskins.
failure_modes_prevented: Drift away from shared art direction
Progression that is only numeric with no staged presentation logic

skills.title: Produce standalone screenshot proof when explicitly requested
use_when: Only when the workflow or task explicitly asks for a standalone screenshot artifact such as screen1.jpg.
skills.intent: Carry forward the embedded single-artifact capture contract as an optional proof mode.
required_actions: Validate the stated upstream transformation prerequisites before capture.
Produce the named screenshot artifact in the requested viewport.
Fail honestly if the prerequisite state is not present.
acceptance_bar: The screenshot artifact is real and current.
Capture requests are not silently faked.
